baseline: D1-D20 built and frozen (commit 04397d9; 585 tests). This graph is the D21 delta only; D1-D20 tasks are deliberately not re-listed.
notes: Two shared hot production files dominate serialisation: ui/chart_panel.py (D21-01,02,03,08,13,15) and ui/main_window.py (D21-05,06,07,10,11,13). touches_files plus the explicit DEPENDS_ON edges keep them in a single serial chain.
ui/visual_conventions.py (D21-04) and services/time_collapse_service.py (D21-14) are [new] prerequisite modules; their consumers depend on them by interface.
D21-13 (D21.10 preview line) is owned by ChartPanel (architecture S14 allows ChartPanel or the alarm overlay), so ui/alarm_overlay.py is touched only by the Phase-6 consumer task D21-16.
D21-17/D21-18 are Build verification tasks; touches_files is empty because they produce only Build-owned docs/build/build_log.md evidence, not source files.
The plan's Phase 5/6 ordering is preserved through the shared-file chains (main_window/chart_panel) plus the D21.2<->D21.4 reconciliation edge D21-02 -> D21-15.

tasks.title: D21.1 — clamp the volume Y minimum at 0
tasks.description: In ui/chart_panel.py enforce a hard volume Y lower bound of 0 via volume_plot.getViewBox().setLimits(yMin=0) so no interactive drag/zoom can move viewRange()[1][0] below 0, while keeping the existing programmatic setRange(yRange=(0, ...)) writes inside the limit and the D8 all-zero [0, 100] floor. Add tests/test_volume_d21.py carrying the D21.1 pre-fix-red/post-fix-green checks.
acceptance_criteria: AC-D21.1.1 — Given the volume pane is visible, When the user drags the volume Y-axis (or otherwise changes the volume Y range by mouse), Then the volume Y minimum never goes below 0 at any time (viewRange()[1][0] >= 0 within float tolerance) and no volume-axis tick below 0 is rendered.

tests.description: Boot an offscreen ChartPanel with bars, assert the volume ViewBox carries setLimits(yMin=0), then drive an interactive downward y change (drag / wheel / setRange with yMin<0 through the bounded path) and assert volume_plot.getViewBox().viewRange()[1][0] >= 0 and the volume axis ticks contain no negative value.
tests.expected_result: The volume Y minimum is clamped at 0 after any user y-interaction; no negative volume tick.

tests.description: With all-zero visible volumes assert the range stays [0, 100] (D8 floor) and that a symbol/timeframe switch re-applies min 0; repeated downward drags stay at 0 and the y-drag still works for the max.
tests.expected_result: All-zero -> [0, 100]; min re-applied on reload; downward drags saturate at 0 while the max remains draggable.

tasks.title: D21.2 — volume Y ceiling = 1.10 x max visible, recomputed on every visible-x change (supersedes D8 nice-max + ESC-007 only-widen)
tasks.description: In ui/chart_panel.py replace the whole-list only-widen nice-max ceiling with _recompute_visible_volume_range() computing 1.10 x max(volume of bars whose x lies in the visible x-range), 0 visible -> VOLUME_NICE_FLOOR (100), wired to price_plot.getViewBox().sigXRangeChanged and re-run on bar updates; retain _nice_volume_max for the all-zero floor / fixtures. Update the D8/ESC-007 lockstep tests (tests/test_volume_linear.py, test_volume_log.py, test_volume_ceiling.py) so the suite is never left contradicting the recorded supersession (R36).
acceptance_criteria: AC-D21.2.1 — Given the volume pane is visible and bars are loaded, When the visible x-range changes (zoom in/out, pan, magnifier area-zoom), Then the volume Y range is [0, 1.10 x max_volume_visible] where max_volume_visible is the largest volume of the bars whose x lies within the currently visible x-range and the min is always 0; all-zero visible -> [0, 100]; this supersedes D8's nice-max ceiling and ESC-007's only-widen rule for zoom while preserving ESC-007's forming-bar no-clip intent via recompute on bar updates.

tests.description: Set a visible x-range covering a known bar subset and assert viewRange()[1] == (0, approx(1.10 * max(visible volumes))) within tolerance; zoom into a lower-volume region and assert the ceiling LOWERS (not only-widen).
tests.expected_result: The volume Y ceiling equals 1.10 x the visible max and follows both directions of a zoom/pan.

tests.description: Assert all-zero visible volumes give [0, 100] (D8 floor), a volume spike just outside the view does not inflate the max, and panning recomputes the ceiling.
tests.expected_result: All-zero -> [0, 100]; out-of-view spike excluded; pan recomputes.

tests.description: Grow the forming last bar intra-bar past the current ceiling and assert the ceiling widens so the bar is not clipped (ESC-007 core intent preserved).
tests.expected_result: Intra-bar growth widens the ceiling; no clipping of the forming bar.

tests.description: Run tests/test_volume_linear.py, tests/test_volume_log.py and tests/test_volume_ceiling.py after their lockstep update and assert zero failures, with no remaining assertion of the D8 nice-max ceiling or the ESC-007 only-widen rule (R36).
tests.expected_result: The three lockstep modules are green and encode the D21.2 rule; no stale nice-max/only-widen assertion remains.

tasks.title: D21.6 — volume pane can grow to >= 360px with a ~200px price-pane minimum
tasks.description: In ui/chart_panel.py add VOLUME_PANE_MAX_HEIGHT = 480 and PRICE_PANE_MIN_HEIGHT = 200, apply volume_plot.setMaximumHeight(VOLUME_PANE_MAX_HEIGHT) and price_plot.setMinimumHeight(PRICE_PANE_MIN_HEIGHT), and tune the vertical splitter sizes/stretch so the volume pane reaches >= 360px while the price pane keeps >= ~200px; the oscillator pane cap is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: AC-D21.6.1 — Given the volume pane is visible, When the user drags the price/volume splitter, Then the volume pane can grow to at least 360px (3x the former 120px cap) and the price pane keeps a minimum of ~200px (the oscillator pane is unaffected).

tests.description: Boot a shown offscreen ChartPanel in a window tall enough, drive the vertical splitter to give the volume pane its maximum, and assert volume_plot.height() >= 360.
tests.expected_result: The volume pane reaches >= 360px.

tests.description: Assert price_plot.height() >= ~200 after the volume pane is grown, and that in a very short window the price minimum wins and the volume target yields without an error.
tests.expected_result: Price pane keeps >= ~200px; short-window precedence is stable.

tests.description: Assert the oscillator pane is unaffected, and that hiding then showing the volume pane (D10) restores the splitter without regressing the price minimum.
tests.expected_result: Oscillator unaffected; hide/show round-trips cleanly; no price-minimum regression.

tasks.title: VIS-D21 — shared primitives: DiagonalStrikeButton (VIS-D21.1) + active highlight (VIS-D21.2)
tasks.description: Create the new leaf module ui/visual_conventions.py holding the shared VIS-D21 primitives: DiagonalStrikeButton (a QPushButton that paints a single cosmetic top-left -> bottom-right line over the text area when struck, auto-striking when a checkable button is unchecked), the VIS-D21.2 toolbar stylesheet constant, and set_button_active(button, active) (Qt dynamic property + repolish). This module is a prerequisite for the watchlist, volume and right-dock consumers.
acceptance_criteria: VIS-D21.1 — Given a hidden/off toggle label/button, Then its text area is rendered with a single straight diagonal line from the top-left to the bottom-right corner, clearly visible against the button background; a checkable DiagonalStrikeButton is struck automatically when unchecked and unstruck when checked.

VIS-D21.2 — Given an active/selected button, Then a persistent highlight (a distinct filled background and/or border) is applied while active and removed when inactive, via a dynamic property that can be asserted independently of painting.

tests.description: Instantiate DiagonalStrikeButton; assert struck is False by default and the painted line appears (paintEvent draws a TL->BR cosmetic line) when struck is set, and that a checkable button auto-strikes when unchecked and unstrikes when checked; assert the button stays clickable while struck.
tests.expected_result: The diagonal strike is present iff the button is struck/hidden and the control remains interactive.

tests.description: Call set_button_active(btn, True) and assert the dynamic 'active' property is True and the resolved style differs from inactive; call set_button_active(btn, False) and assert the property is cleared and the style returns to the inactive form.
tests.expected_result: Active style differs from inactive and is applied while active / removed when inactive.

tests.description: Assert the VIS-D21.2 stylesheet constant targets the toolbar objectName and the :checked / [active="true"] selectors, so it is scroll-position independent in the D19 wrapper.
tests.expected_result: The shared stylesheet applies to the toolbar controls independent of scroll position.

tasks.title: D21.8 — Alarm Mode highlight + status message that persists until the mode ends
tasks.description: In ui/main_window.py give alarm_mode_btn the VIS-D21.2 active highlight while Alarm Mode is on and change _on_alarm_mode_toggled to show the status-bar message with no timeout (instead of the current 4000ms), clearing/replacing it when Alarm Mode ends (button off, alarm placed, drawing tool selected, or mode otherwise exited) so it does not permanently mask later messages.

tests.description: Activate Alarm Mode, wait/advance past 4s and assert the alarm-mode status text is still shown; deactivate and assert it is no longer shown.

tasks.title: D21.12 — Volume button struck when the volume pane is hidden

tasks.title: D21.5 — configurable watchlist columns (add/remove/rearrange, Symbol kept, persisted)
tasks.description: In ui/watchlist_panel.py replace the fixed 7-column index schema with a COLUMN_DEFS field-key model: an ordered active-field list, cells built per active field, and _set_cell/on_tick_price/on_tick_size/_on_cell_double_clicked addressing by field key; force Symbol present; add a right-click header popup (checkable add/remove + move left/right) that rebuilds the table; and persist the layout in QSettings key 'watchlist/columns' with a sanitised restore on launch.
acceptance_criteria: AC-D21.5.1 — Given the watchlist is visible, When the user right-clicks a column header, Then a popup opens offering to add, remove and rearrange columns.

AC-D21.5.2 — Given the popup, Then the addable set is the existing 7 columns (Symbol, Last, Bid, Ask, Chg, Chg %, Vol); 'add' means re-showing a previously removed column (no new data fields are introduced).
AC-D21.5.3 — Given a column is to be removed, Then the Symbol column cannot be removed (it always remains in the layout).

AC-D21.5.4 — Given a changed column set/order, Then the table updates immediately to the chosen columns in the chosen order, each cell value remains bound to the correct field, and the layout is persisted across restarts (restored on launch).

tests.description: Boot an offscreen WatchlistPanel, invoke the header context-menu handler, and assert a popup is offered with add, remove and rearrange affordances.
tests.expected_result: A right-click on the header opens the add/remove/rearrange popup.

tests.description: Assert the addable field set equals exactly the existing 7 fields and that removing then re-adding a column restores it; no new field key is introduced.
tests.expected_result: Addable set == existing 7; add == re-show a removed column.

tests.description: Attempt to remove Symbol and assert it is blocked and still present; assert all other columns can be removed leaving only Symbol.
tests.expected_result: Symbol removal is blocked; Symbol always remains.

tests.description: Remove and reorder columns, then deliver a live tick and assert each value lands in the correct field cell (field-identity binding, not index); assert D14 double-click still resolves the Symbol row after a reorder.
tests.expected_result: Immediate correct update after reorder/remove; field binding preserved; D14 still works.

tests.description: Persist a changed layout to QSettings('watchlist/columns'), reconstruct the panel, and assert the same ordered column set is restored; assert unknown keys are dropped and symbol is forced present.
tests.expected_result: Layout survives a simulated restart with sanitised restore.

tasks.title: D21.11 — one 'Watchlist' label: in-panel header becomes the hide/show toggle
tasks.description: In ui/main_window.py and ui/watchlist_panel.py delete the duplicate QDockWidget('Watchlist') title and use the in-panel header strip as the dock's title-bar widget (setTitleBarWidget), with its label turned into a DiagonalStrikeButton('Watchlist'). AC-D21.11.2 — Given the watchlist is hidden via that button, Then the retained button stays visible (it must not disappear with the dock) and is rendered with the VIS-D21.1 diagonal strike-through; clicking it again shows the watchlist (strike removed).
AC-D21.11.3 — Given the watchlist is hidden/collapsed, Then the collapsed state still shows the button.

tests.description: Boot an offscreen MainWindow and assert exactly one visible 'Watchlist' label exists across the dock title and the panel; assert the dock's title-bar widget is the in-panel header strip and the header control is a clickable toggle button.
tests.expected_result: Exactly one Watchlist label; header strip is the title-bar widget and a toggle button.

tests.description: Click the toggle to hide; assert the panel body is hidden but the header/button stays visible and struck; click again and assert the body is shown and the strike removed.
tests.expected_result: Toggle collapses the body while the struck button stays visible; re-click restores.

tests.description: Assert that in the collapsed state the button is still visible and reachable, and that the dock remains movable/floatable via the title-bar widget; assert the D17/D18 width model still holds when hidden.

tasks.title: D21.13 — Active Trader / Account Summary hide/show toggles with in-height and horizontal collapse
tasks.description: In ui/main_window.py, ui/active_trader_panel.py and ui/active_portfolio_panel.py make the right dock's title bar a DiagonalStrikeButton('Active Trader') and the portfolio summary_label a DiagonalStrikeButton('Account Summary'); hiding a panel hides its body keeping its button, and the other expands. When both are hidden the dock collapses horizontally to the button strip by (a) relaxing right_dock.setMinimumWidth(RIGHT_DOCK_COLLAPSED_MIN_WIDTH) and (b) explicitly calling _resize_docks_guarded([right_dock], [collapsed_width]), while _apply_dock_widths treats the region as collapsed/hidden for the cross-clamp; showing either panel restores RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH and the normal B3 cross-clamp, and _on_dom_toggled stays the whole-region toggle without resetting per-panel state.
acceptance_criteria: AC-D21.13.1 — Given the right dock is visible, Then 'Active Trader' = the right dock's title bar and 'Account Summary' = the portfolio's summary label, and both become toggle buttons: the Active Trader button hides/shows the Active Trader panel, and the Account Summary button hides/shows the Account Summary (portfolio) panel.
AC-D21.13.2 — Given one of the two panels is hidden, Then that panel collapses in height to just its button, and the other panel expands to fill the vacated vertical space.
AC-D21.13.3 — Given both panels are hidden, Then the right dock collapses horizontally to the minimum width required to show the two buttons (the chart reclaims the width).
AC-D21.13.4 — Given a panel is hidden, Then its button shows the VIS-D21.1 diagonal strike-through; when shown, the strike is removed.

tests.description: Boot an offscreen MainWindow; assert the right dock title-bar widget contains a DiagonalStrikeButton('Active Trader') and the portfolio summary is a DiagonalStrikeButton('Account Summary'); clicking each toggles the matching panel body.
tests.expected_result: Both labels are toggle buttons mapped to the correct panels.

tests.description: Hide one panel and assert it collapses to just its button while the other panel's height grows to fill the vacated space; re-show and assert the original split is restored.
tests.expected_result: One-hidden collapses in height and the other expands; re-show restores.

tests.description: Hide both panels; assert right_dock.minimumWidth() is relaxed to RIGHT_DOCK_COLLAPSED_MIN_WIDTH (below RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH), the dock width is explicitly reduced to the button strip via _resize_docks_guarded, and the chart keeps >= CHART_MIN_WIDTH; show a panel and assert the 200px minimum and the normal cross-clamp are restored.
tests.expected_result: Both-hidden collapses horizontally to the button strip with the chart minimum held; showing restores the 200px minimum and cross-clamp.

tests.description: Assert each panel's button reports struck iff its panel is hidden, and the strike is removed when shown.
tests.expected_result: Strike reflects each panel's hidden state.

tests.description: Exercise _on_dom_toggled: assert it hides/shows the whole region and does not reset per-panel hidden states; assert the collapsed region is treated as hidden by _apply_dock_widths so the watchlist regains its own cap.
tests.expected_result: DOM toggle remains whole-region; per-panel state persists; cross-clamp consistent.

tasks.title: D21.4 — pure time-collapse service (coverage-adjusted predicate, 1 day identity)
tasks.description: Create the new pure, Qt-free services/time_collapse_service.py: build_collapse_map(bars, timeframe, ext_hours) -> TimeCollapseMap with to_display(ts), to_ts(x), x_values, is_identity; and gap_is_non_trading(a, b, ext_hours, bar_period) returning True (collapse) iff market_calendar.session_windows(a + bar_period, b, ext_hours) is empty, with bar_period = TIMEFRAME_SECONDS[timeframe]. 1 day is the identity map. Bar.ts is never mutated.
acceptance_criteria: AC-D21.4.1 (predicate) — Given consecutive bars a < b on an intraday timeframe, Then gap_is_non_trading(a, b, ext_hours, bar_period) is True (collapse) iff market_calendar.session_windows(a + bar_period, b, ext_hours) is empty; the ordinary RTH overnight, extended-hours overnight, weekend and holiday gaps collapse while a within-session hole and a missing full trading session stay visible.
AC-D21.4.2 — Given the timeframe is 1 day, Then build_collapse_map is the identity map (is_identity True).
AC-D21.4.4 — Given a genuine trading-session data hole (D16), Then it is not collapsed and collapse remains a display-only transform that neither fabricates nor drops trading-session bars.

tests.description: Against the real services.market_calendar.session_windows with bar_period=300 assert the eight boundary cases: RTH overnight Fri 15:55->Mon 09:30 collapses, ext overnight Fri 19:55->Mon 04:00 collapses, weekend collapses, holiday collapses, within-session hole 11:00->13:00 is kept, missing full session (Mon close->Wed open) is kept, partial half-day afternoon hole is kept, adjacent bars collapse (no-op).
tests.expected_result: All between-session gaps collapse; within-session holes and missing sessions stay visible.

tests.description: Build the map for the 1 day timeframe and assert is_identity is True and to_display(ts) == ts for the bar timestamps.
tests.expected_result: 1 day is a no-op identity map.

tests.description: Assert x_values are strictly increasing, to_display/to_ts round-trip for bar timestamps, and within-session adjacent bars keep their normal spacing (only between-session gaps are removed).
tests.expected_result: Monotonic display-x, correct round-trip, within-session spacing preserved.
